name: Question 2
worked_solution:
The power set of $T,$ denoted $P(T),$ is the set that contains every possible subset of $T,$ including the empty set $∅.$

So, let's list all possible subsets of $T$ using a tree diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14095809/assets/1ef8e646081305399cddbf6908bd8415d908dab3e9bb0e371d68b33e62084774.png)

According to our diagram, the subsets of $T$ are

$$
∅={},\,{k},\,{m},\,{o},\,{k,m},\,{k,o},\,{m,o},\,{k,m,o}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(T)={∅,{k},{m},{o},{k,m},{k,o},{m,o},{k,m,o}}.
$$

Question 2
?

If T={k,m,o}, then P(T)=

a
{∅,{k},{m},{o},{k,m},{k,o},{m,o},{k,m,o}}
b
{∅,{k},{m},{o},{k,m},{k,o},{m,o}}
c
{∅,k,m,o,{k,m},{k,o},{m,o},{k,m,o}}
d
{{k},{m},{o},{k,m,o}}
e
{∅,{k,m,o}}
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The power set of T, denoted P(T), is the set that contains every possible subset of T, including the empty set ∅.

So, let's list all possible subsets of T using a tree diagram.

According to our diagram, the subsets of T are

∅={},{k},{m},{o},{k,m},{k,o},{m,o},{k,m,o}.

Therefore, we have

P(T)={∅,{k},{m},{o},{k,m},{k,o},{m,o},{k,m,o}}.
